description.narrative: Jan Schoemaker B.V. or JS Cocoa was founded in 1923 by the brothers Schoenmaker. They discovered a niche market for unconventional cocoa raw materials such as fat and cocoa-specialised production techniques to extract this fat from unusual (waste) beans. Schoenmaker has been using mechanical and solvent extraction techniques for the extraction of cocoa fat since 1925 and started refining cocoa fat for the production of refined and deodorised cocoa butter in 1958. The company has a production facility in Zaandam, the Netherlands, and a subsidiary company, RESIGHA, in Ghana.RESIGHA focuses exclusively on the purchase and export of poor quality beans to the JS Cocoa production facility in the Netherlands. With more than 100 years of industry experience, JS Cocoa is recognised as a leading producer of cocoa ingredients. The company uses cocoa residual flows from cocoa and chocolate industry to produce and sell cocoa butter and cocoa powder.The regulatory landscape surrounding cocoa is changing rapidly, both from the European Union (EU), like the Deforestation-free products (EUDR) and the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), but also from Ghana itself, where people want to achieve a shift to local production. Partly because of this, JS Cocoa wants to investigate to what extent production in Ghana can be efficient and effective. In addition, it is important whether it is technically and financially feasible to locally process some of the off-grade beans from Ghana. JS Cocoa also pays attention to development impact with production that has the most positive impact on farmers and corporations locally. They therefore want to conduct the research for three production variants, namely1. large-scale production at one location,2. containerised production at farmers or3. a hybrid form, in which part of the production takes place at farmers and part centrally. All production will be on an expelling basis.
